title: Ensuring Fair Play
body:
# Ensuring Fair Play

Raiders,

Anti-cheat at Embark is a studio-wide effort that protects every player across our games. With ARC Raiders Riven Tides now live, we want to lay out where things currently stand, what we are building, and how we approach the tougher challenges of fair play in ARC Raiders.

# **How We Protect Fair Play**

Our anti-cheat system pairs kernel-level protection from Easy Anti-Cheat with detection powered by machine-learning (ML) models. These models are trained on a steady stream of player telemetry. Additional layers of protection exist behind these, but we keep the details private for operational security reasons.

Kernel-level detection is essential because most commercial cheats run at that level. Without this kind of access, we would have very limited visibility into the tools causing the most harm. Right now, we are testing a new kernel-level solution that we expect will improve both the accuracy and precision of detection across Speranza and the Rust Belt.

On the machine-learning front, analyzing input telemetry has proven to be one of our strongest tools. We have trained and rolled out a group of models focused specifically on this task, and we have partnered with Anybrain on this research from the very beginning.

# **Accessibility and Intent**

Handling accessibility devices remains one of the toughest challenges in anti-cheat work. Players who need this equipment must be able to play, but since official solutions tend to be costly, some players turn to lesser-known devices to get the same result. Unfortunately, these same tools can be misused for cheating.

What matters most to us is intent. Our systems examine telemetry and communication patterns to tell legitimate accessibility use apart from abuse, so that players relying on these devices can continue playing without issue. We keep refining this process, and we remain committed to the work, along with the progress we have seen so far.

Official devices from major platforms are widely recognized and common, which lets us detect them accurately and understand the intent behind their use. Our partners at Anybrain continue to grow their knowledge of different accessibility hardware. This helps us detect a wider range of devices and refine how we handle various use cases, making our ML detection smarter, more dependable, and more accessible over time.

# **How Ban Appeals Work**

A person on our team reviews every ban appeal. This process is not automated, and we continue to improve it as we learn more from the cases we encounter. A fair and accurate appeals process is important to us across all our games, and we treat it as an ongoing investment rather than something we consider complete.

We understand it can be frustrating to wait for a response and to receive the pre-written replies our agents must use to stay consistent. Even so, we examine each case carefully to protect fair gameplay and to test and improve the systems and models we have built to keep the game fair and enjoyable.

Stay tuned for more updates from us soon!

Until then, we'll see you Topside! (We've got eyes everywhere) The Anti-Cheat Team
